newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes stronger on dollar influx.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes stronger on dollar influx.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended earlier firmness towards the close on Monday to pierce resistance at 7.90 per dollar as domestic and foreign players stepped in to sell dollars, traders said.
"Local banks that had gone long dollars on Friday and foreign investors stepping in flooded the market with dollars," said a trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 3.1 centavos firmer, at 7.8900/7.8940 and 7.8840/7.8890 per dollar respectively.
Same-day peso contracts earlier closed 1.3 centavos softer at 7.9000/7.9100.
Dealers said trading was light as the market awaited the announcement of November inflation figures, expected shortly after the close of trade.

A Reuters survey MXAAP of financial professionals showed an average forecast of 1.56 percent for November inflation. Some foreign exchange dealers said, however, they were expecting inflation to rise to 1.8 percent. Inflation in October was 1.25 percent.
Some dealers put the inflow of dollars from foreign dealers down to expectations that bellwether 28-day Cetes rates would gain at the central bank's auction of government securities later today.
A Reuters survey of money market traders showed they forecast an assignment rate of 27.85 percent on average for 28-day Cetes, 83 basis points above last week's rate.
The auction was moved forward as the working week will be cut short by a holiday honouring Our Lady of Guadalupe on Thursday.
Dealers saw support for the 48-hour peso at 7.88 per dollar.
